# Tools and code

This page describes how a workflow calls HTTP APIs and runs Python. Read [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) first.

Statements marked "verified in a working builder" come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API. The workflow has code nodes, `api_call` tools, post-hooks and transitions on tool results. Its agent passed its practice cases. Statements marked "seen in a trial call" come from the event log of a simulation call made with that builder.

## Tool function shape

Every external action is a **tool function**. The shape is the same wherever you attach it.

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
  "function": {
    "name": "lookup_order",
    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
    "description": "Look up one order. CALL it when the caller asks about a specific order.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/orders/lookup" },
        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
        "headers": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } }
        },
        "body": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "customer_id": { "type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}" },
            "order_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Order number, digits only", "default": "{{order_number}}" }
          },
          "required": ["order_number"]
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | Always `"function"` |
| `function.name` | Tool name. The model calls it by this name. Result variables are named after it |
| `function.handler` | Which runtime executes the tool. See the table below |
| `function.description` | Read by the dialogue model when the tool is in `tools`. Ignored in `pre_actions` |
| `function.parameters` | JSON-schema object. `properties` holds the parameters |
| `config.timeoutMs` | Timeout of one attempt, in milliseconds |
| `config.maxRetries` | Tool-level retries of a failed call |
| `config.interruptible` | `false` makes the tool run in the background. See "Background tools" |
| `config.alwaysRunsAt` | Makes the tool a lifecycle tool. See "Lifecycle tools" |
| `response_mapping` | Tool level, for tools in `tools`. Maps the result to variables |
| `pre_process_code` | Python hook that runs before the call |
| `post_process_code` | Python hook that runs after the call |

| Handler | Runs |
|---|---|
| `__function__:api_call` | An HTTP request |
| `__function__:code_exec` | A Python snippet in a sandbox |
| `__function__:end_call` | Hangs up. Used in the `terminal` of an `end_call` node |

Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.

`api_call` parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
| `method` | HTTP method |
| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |

## How a parameter gets its value

One key decides, per parameter: `default`.

| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
|---|---|---|
| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
| no `default` | The model | Yes |
| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |

Rules:

- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.

The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.

Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.

Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.

### `api_call` body field rules

- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
- Give each leaf its own `default`.
- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.

A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.

### When a baked variable has no value

| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
|---|---|---|
| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |

Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.

### Constrain model-filled parameters

When a value must be one of a known set, do not use a free string. The model sometimes invents a value that looks plausible.

- Use an `enum` on the leaf, and list the values in the `description` as well.
- Or use a `number` that is an index into a list, with the valid range in the description. A pre-hook or the backend turns the index into the real value.
- If neither is possible, name the exact source in the description and tell the model to copy the value unchanged.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "queue": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Team that takes over. One of: billing, delivery, returns.",
      "enum": ["billing", "delivery", "returns"],
      "default": "{{queue}}"
    }
  },
  "required": ["queue"]
}
```

## `pre_actions` versus `tools`

The placement decides who fires the call.

| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |

The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.

**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.

**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.

Differences in behaviour:

| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
|---|---|---|
| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |

To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.

### A `pre_actions` node

```json
{
  "name": "fetch_order",
  "node_type": "api_request",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "present",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
      "function": {
        "name": "get_order",
        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
        "description": "Get the order.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/get_order" },
            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
            "headers": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } } },
            "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string", "default": "{{order_number}}" } }, "required": [] }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "present", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

The last `always` transition is mandatory. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.

### Tool descriptions

In `tools`, the `description` decides whether the model calls the tool.

- Write it as an instruction with the trigger: "CALL it every time the caller gives an order number."
- A plain description such as "Looks up an order" lets the model acknowledge the request in words and never call the tool. That is the most common failure of nodes with many tools.
- If two tools could match, say which one not to use and name the other.
- In `task_message`, put the tool rules before long reference text and state: when a rule says to use a tool, call the tool.
- The working builder also tells the model to call one tool per message and to speak after every tool result. Verified in a working builder. In a trial call a model turn with no text and no tool call produced the error event "The model returned no speakable content".

A tool is available only in the nodes that list it. Seen in a trial call: the model called a tool that the current node did not list. The result was the text "The function `<name>` is not currently available."

## `response_mapping`

`response_mapping` copies values from a call result into named variables. It needs no model call.

```json
{
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" },
    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | Dot path into the tool result |
| `variable` | Name of the variable to set |

### Placement

- For a tool in `tools`: inside the tool object, next to `function` and `config`.
- For `pre_actions`: at the **node level**. A `response_mapping` nested inside a `pre_actions` entry is ignored and the variable never appears.

`extraction_schema` follows the same placement rule if you use it on a call result.

### Where a result lands (trial findings)

Seen in a trial call: the result of an `api_call` is an envelope around the HTTP response.

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": { "ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3 },
  "message": "Successfully executed POST request",
  "status_code": 200,
  "header": { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
}
```

`data` is the JSON body the API returned. `header` holds the HTTP response headers.

The engine also writes every result into the variable table by itself, flattened with dots. You do not need a mapping for these. For a tool named `check_answer` whose API returned `{"ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3}`, the trial call's variable table held:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `check_answer_args.<field>` | Each argument the model sent |
| `check_answer_response.status` | `success` |
| `check_answer_response.data.ok` | `true` (a string) |
| `check_answer_response.data.verified` | `true` (a string) |
| `check_answer_response.data.attempts_left` | `3` |
| `check_answer_response.message` | `Successfully executed POST request` |
| `check_answer_response.status_code` | `200` |
| `check_answer_response.header.<Header-Name>` | One variable per response header |
| `check_answer_status_code` | `200` |
| `check_answer_success_count` | Number of successful calls so far |

Each call of the same tool overwrites the previous `_args` and `_response` values.

### Which mapping paths work

- **Start the path at the envelope, with `data.`**. If the API returns `{"ok": true}`, map `data.ok`. If it returns `{"products": [...]}`, map `data.products`. Verified in a working builder, on a tool-level mapping and on a node-level mapping.
- A path without the `data.` prefix (for the same body: `ok`) is not confirmed. A smaller example builder uses it. In an early trial call the mapped variables stayed unset and the transitions on them never fired. The mapping paths of that call are not recorded. The builder that passed uses `data.` paths.
- The flattened key can be used directly as a transition variable: `check_answer_response.data.verified`. Verified in a working builder, which tests the mapped variable and the flattened key in the same OR group as a safeguard.
- Booleans arrive as strings. The trial call showed `true` in lower case in the flattened keys. Test both `"true"` and `"True"`, or map a string field.
- A mapped list or object: the exact form it has later inside `vars` is not confirmed. The working builder reads it defensively. It accepts a list, a JSON string, and flattened keys.

## Routing on tool results

Routing runs again after a tool result arrives. A transition on a result variable fires in the same turn, before any further model turn. Seen in a trial call.

```json
{
  "transitions": [
    {
      "target_node": "load_order",
      "description": "The check passed",
      "condition": {
        "logic": "or",
        "conditions": [
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- On a passthrough node, end with an `always` transition so that a failed or empty response does not deadlock.
- Use a tool result to leave a conversation node. The pattern "a closing tool sets a variable, a transition on that variable leads to an `end_call` node" is verified in a working builder.
- To leave a node that carries out an action, do not re-test the user's earlier intent with `matches_intent`. The router looks at the latest user message and can route away before the tool was called. Extract a follow-up enum with a default such as `stay`, and branch with `equals`.

### Success and failure counters

The engine keeps two integer variables per call target. No mapping is needed.

| Placement | Variables |
|---|---|
| `pre_actions` node | `<nodeId>_success_count`, `<nodeId>_failure_count` |
| Tool in `tools` with handler `api_call` | `<toolName>_success_count`, `<toolName>_failure_count` |

Seen in a trial call: `check_answer_success_count` was `2` after two successful calls, and a code node named `setup` produced `setup_success_count` with the value `1`.

```json
{
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "give_up", "description": "The lookup failed three times", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "lookup_order_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 2 } ] } },
    { "target_node": "ask_again", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

### `suppress_tool_results`

A node-level boolean for nodes that run API calls. With `true` the dialogue model sees only a short `{status: "success"}` summary in place of the raw response. Variables are still mapped and routing still sees them. Use it for large responses, or when the mapped variables already hold everything the model needs.

### Background tools

A tool with `"config": {"interruptible": false}` runs in the background. A user interruption does not cancel it. Its result arrives one or more turns later. The mapped variables, the `_response` keys and the counters are filled as usual, but not in the same turn. A transition that reads them right after the call can find them unset. Gate on the variable with `is_set`.

## Retries and timeouts

| Setting | Where | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `timeoutMs` | `config` | not documented | Time limit of one attempt, in milliseconds |
| `maxRetries` | `config` | not documented | Tool-level retries after a failed response |
| `connect_retries` | `parameters.properties`, as a baked parameter | `2` | Retries when the connection could not be established |
| `timeout_ms` | `code_exec` parameter | `30000` | Time limit of a code snippet |

`connect_retries` in detail:

- It retries only failures to establish the connection: connection refused, or reset during the TCP or TLS handshake. The request never reached the server, so a repeat is safe even for POST.
- HTTP error statuses and timeouts are not retried by it.
- Hard cap `5`. `0` means a single attempt.
- Back-off is 150 ms times the attempt number, with a new connection each time.
- All attempts share one 30 second budget for the request.
- Declare it next to `url` and `method`: `"connect_retries": {"type": "number", "default": 0}`. It is not a `config` field.

The working builder sets `maxRetries` to `0` on tools that write data and to `2` on its read-only `pre_actions` call. A retried write can record the same thing twice if the API is not idempotent.

## Pre and post Python hooks

An `api_call` tool can carry two Python snippets. They run on the server, in a sandbox, right before and right after the call. They are top-level fields of the tool object.

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 0 },
  "function": {
    "name": "check_answer",
    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
    "description": "Check one answer. CALL it every time the caller answers the question.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/check_answer" },
        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
        "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string", "description": "The caller's answer", "default": "{{answer}}" } }, "required": ["answer"] }
      }
    }
  },
  "pre_process_code": "vars['member_code'] = str(vars.get('member_code') or '').strip().upper()",
  "post_process_code": "try:\n    if isinstance(result, dict):\n        result.pop('header', None)\n        d = result.get('data')\n        if isinstance(d, dict):\n            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Ask the next question.' if d.get('verified') else 'Ask the same question again.'\nexcept Exception:\n    pass\n"
}
```

| Hook | Names available | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `pre_process_code` | `vars`: mutable dict that fills the `{{var}}` placeholders of the request. `config`: the substituted request with `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body` | Clean a value, or rewrite the whole request |
| `post_process_code` | `result`: the tool result, mutable | Reshape, shorten or extend the result |

Documented behaviour:

- The post-hook runs before `response_mapping` and extraction see the result.
- An empty or whitespace-only string means no hook.
- Hooks are honoured only on `api_call` tools (and on the integration and knowledge search handlers). The platform removes them from any other handler when the workflow is saved.
- In a pre-hook, setting `config['body']` to a string sends that string as the raw body, with no JSON encoding. Set the `Content-Type` header yourself in that case.

### What `result` looks like in a post-hook

The internal reference shows `result` as the response body. A working builder shows otherwise. Verified in a working builder:

- For an `api_call`, `result` is the envelope described above: a dict with `status`, `data`, `message`, `status_code` and `header`. The API's JSON body is `result["data"]`.
- A key that the hook adds inside `result["data"]` reaches the dialogue model as part of the tool result. The working builder adds a `what_to_do_next` sentence there, and its prompt tells the model to obey it.
- `result.pop("header", None)` removes the response headers. The working builder does this on every tool, so that headers do not take up space in the model's context.
- Mapping paths still start with `data.` when a post-hook is present.

The working builder writes every hook inside `try` and `except Exception: pass` and checks types with `isinstance` before use. What the platform does when a hook raises is not documented.

Seen in a test on 10 October: a post-hook can read call variables and write new variables, and a later pre-hook reads them. Not confirmed: whether a change to `result` also changes the flattened `<tool>_response.*` variables.

## Code nodes and `code_exec`

A `code` node runs a Python snippet when it is entered. The snippet is a `code_exec` function in `pre_actions`.

```json
{
  "name": "compute_delivery",
  "node_type": "code",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "tell_delivery",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "code_exec",
        "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "code": { "type": "string", "default": "import datetime\ntry:\n    start = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('shipped_on'))[:10])\n    eta = start + datetime.timedelta(days=3)\n    vars['delivery_day'] = eta.isoformat()\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'known'\nexcept Exception:\n    vars['delivery_day'] = ''\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'unknown'\n" },
            "timeout_ms": { "type": "number", "default": 10000 }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "tell_delivery", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `code` | The Python source, as a baked `default` string |
| `timeout_ms` | Time limit in milliseconds. Default `30000` |

### Reading and writing variables

- The snippet gets a dict named `vars`. It holds the current workflow variables.
- Read with `vars.get("name")`. A variable that was never set is absent.
- Write with `vars["name"] = value`. Every key the snippet assigns becomes a workflow variable.

Verified in a working builder:

- Call variables are in `vars`. The builder reads `vars.get("now")`, a call variable passed with the simulation.
- The result of an earlier `api_request` node is reachable from `vars` in a later code node. The builder looks for it under the mapped variable name first and under the flattened result keys second. Which of the two held the data is not recorded.
- A string written to `vars["date_facts"]` in a code node resolves as `{{date_facts}}` in the `task_message` of later conversation nodes. Multi-line strings work.
- The standard modules `json`, `re` and `datetime` can be imported.
- The same snippet can run in two code nodes at different points of the call. The later run sees the variables added in between.

### What a code node returns

Seen in a trial call: the result of a successful `code_exec` is

```json
{ "status": "success", "data": null, "message": "Code executed successfully", "status_code": 200 }
```

The snippet's output is not in `data`. Its values reach the workflow only through `vars`. After a code node named `setup` ran, the variable table held:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| each key the snippet wrote, for example `date_facts` | the value, with source `tool_result` and source node `setup` |
| `setup_response.status` | `success` |
| `setup_response.data` | `null` |
| `setup_response.message` | `Code executed successfully` |
| `setup_response.status_code` | `200` |
| `setup_status_code` | `200` |
| `setup_success_count` | `1` |

For a code node the automatic keys are named after the **node**, not after `code_exec`.

### Rules for snippets

- **Do not write `{{` or `}}` in the code.** The internal sources disagree on whether the `code` field is templated. One says it is exempt. Another says placeholders are resolved when the code runs and an unset one is left as literal text, which breaks the Python. The working builder removes every `{{` and `}}` from generated code (a nested dict literal such as `{'a': {'b': 1}}` ends in `}}`) and reads all values from `vars`.
- **Never let a snippet raise.** Wrap the body in `try` and `except`, and write a fallback value for every variable that a later prompt or condition reads. A prompt that references an unset variable shows the literal placeholder to the model.
- **Write strings for routing flags**, such as `known` and `unknown`. Do not route on a Python boolean. See "Do not route on a boolean" in workflow-format.md.
- Keep snippets fast. They block the conversation.
- Do arithmetic, date calculation and counting in code, and give the model the finished facts as text. Verified in a working builder: it computes a block of date facts in a code node and places it in the prompts.
- Treat a code node like an API node: `passthrough: true`, a `passthrough_default_transition`, and a last `always` transition.

### Sandbox limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Time | `timeout_ms`, default `30000` |
| Modules | `json`, `re` and `datetime` are verified in a working builder. The full list is not documented |
| Network and file access | Not documented |
| Memory and output size | Not documented |

### `code_exec` as a tool

`code_exec` can also be a tool in the `tools` array of a conversation node, called by the model. Its parameters are top-level arguments, declared without `default` so the model fills them. For such a tool the `code` field resolves `{{var}}` when the tool is called, against the current variable table. The working builder does not use this form, so nothing about it is verified here.

## Lifecycle tools

A tool whose `config.alwaysRunsAt` is a non-empty list is never shown to the model. The engine fires it at a fixed point of the call.

| Value | When |
|---|---|
| `start_of_call` | During call setup, before the first turn |
| `end_of_call` | After the call has ended |
| `each_turn` | Accepted by the schema but not implemented. It never fires |

Put a lifecycle tool that must run on every call into the workflow's top-level `tools` array.

```json
{
  "initial_node": "greeting",
  "nodes": {},
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "config": { "alwaysRunsAt": ["end_of_call"] },
      "function": {
        "name": "push_call_result",
        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/call-results" },
            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
            "body": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "summary": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.analysis.summary}}" },
                "reason": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.call_end_reason}}" }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- A workflow-level tool without `alwaysRunsAt` never runs and the model never sees it.
- A lifecycle tool in a node's `tools` runs for `start_of_call` only on the `initial_node`, and for `end_of_call` only on the node in which the call ended.
- If a `{{var}}` parameter is still unresolved, one model call fills the parameters. If everything resolves, the handler runs directly.
- `response_mapping` is applied for `start_of_call`. It is not applied for `end_of_call`.
- At the end of a call the order is: call analysis, then `end_of_call` tools, then success-criteria judging. An `end_of_call` tool can use `{{call.analysis.summary}}`, `{{call.analysis.structured_data_str}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason_category}}`, `{{call.call_tags}}` and `{{call.duration}}`.
- A malformed lifecycle tool is dropped at run time without an error. Validate with a dry run (api.md).

## Tool results and the next turn

After a tool call returns, the model sees the result and has to produce the next turn itself. Two things were seen in practice runs with the hackathon's agent model:

- **The agent says nothing after the tool call.** The result arrives, no assistant message follows, and the simulated customer hangs up after waiting. It happens more often when the result is bare data such as `{"ok": true, "verified": true}`.
- **The agent ignores a negative result.** For example it reads `"verified": false` and moves on to the next question as if the answer had passed.

What fixed both in a working builder (verified, see the post-hook section above): a post-hook on the tool that adds one plain instruction line to the result before the model sees it, for example a `what_to_do_next` field that says what the answer means and what to say or call next. The model then has something to act on.

Also say it in the step's prompt: after every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing.

## Checklist

- Fixed values use `default`, never `const`.
- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties` with its own `default`, `description` and `enum`.
- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes. `pre_actions` only on `api_request` and `code` nodes.
- `response_mapping` on the tool for `tools`, on the node for `pre_actions`.
- Mapping paths start with `data.`.
- Booleans from results are tested as `"true"` and `"True"`, or replaced by string fields.
- Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.

def save_workflow(slot, workflow, state_file=".freya-agents.json"):
    """Create the workflow the first time, update the same one afterwards. Use this in your builder.

    `slot` is your own label, for example the brief's file name. A workspace holds a limited number of workflows,
    so a builder that creates a new one on every run stops working after a few runs."""
    import pathlib
    f = pathlib.Path(state_file); state = json.loads(f.read_text()) if f.exists() else {}
    if slot in state:
        state[slot]["version"] = update_workflow(state[slot]["workflow_id"], workflow); f.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
    else:
        state[slot] = create_workflow(f"{slot} {time.strftime('%m%d-%H%M%S')}", workflow); f.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
    return state[slot]
def validate_workflow(name, workflow): return api("POST", "/api/v2/workflow", {"name": name, "workflow": workflow}, dryRun="true")
def update_workflow(workflow_id, workflow):
    """Update a workflow and publish the new version. Returns the published version number.

    An update alone only saves a new, unpublished version. Simulations and calls keep running the published one,
    so an update that is not published tests your old phone agent."""
    api("PUT", f"/api/v2/workflow/{workflow_id}", {"workflow": workflow})
    # The platform fills in a default agent_config. If its model is not the event's model, a simulation still runs
    # (it overrides the model), but a chat turn or a real call cannot start. Set the model and save once more.
    w = api("GET", f"/api/v2/workflow/{workflow_id}", workspaceId=workspace_id())["workflow"]["workflow"]
    ac = w.get("agent_config") or {}; llm = ac.get("llmConfig") or {}
    if (llm.get("provider"), llm.get("model")) != (AGENT_LLM["provider"], AGENT_LLM["model"]):
        ac["llmConfig"] = {**llm, **AGENT_LLM}; api("PUT", f"/api/v2/workflow/{workflow_id}", {"workflow": {**w, "agent_config": ac}})
    vs = api("GET", f"/api/v2/versions/workflow/{workflow_id}", workspaceId=workspace_id())["versions"]
    newest = max(vs, key=lambda v: v["versionNumber"])
    if not newest.get("isPublished"): api("POST", f"/api/v2/versions/workflow/{workflow_id}/publish", {"versionId": newest["id"]})
    return newest["versionNumber"]

def save_workflow(slot, workflow, state_file=".freya-agents.json"):
    """Create the workflow the first time, update the same one afterwards. Use this in your builder.

    `slot` is your own label, for example the brief's file name. A workspace holds a limited number of workflows,
    so a builder that creates a new one on every run stops working after a few runs."""
    import pathlib
    f = pathlib.Path(state_file); state = json.loads(f.read_text()) if f.exists() else {}
    if slot in state:
        state[slot]["version"] = update_workflow(state[slot]["workflow_id"], workflow); f.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
    else:
        state[slot] = create_workflow(f"{slot} {time.strftime('%m%d-%H%M%S')}", workflow); f.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
    return state[slot]
def validate_workflow(name, workflow): return api("POST", "/api/v2/workflow", {"name": name, "workflow": workflow}, dryRun="true")
def update_workflow(workflow_id, workflow):
    """Update a workflow and publish the new version. Returns the published version number.

    An update alone only saves a new, unpublished version. Simulations and calls keep running the published one,
    so an update that is not published tests your old phone agent."""
    api("PUT", f"/api/v2/workflow/{workflow_id}", {"workflow": workflow})
    # The platform fills in a default agent_config. If its model is not the event's model, a simulation still runs
    # (it overrides the model), but a chat turn or a real call cannot start. Set the model and save once more.
    w = api("GET", f"/api/v2/workflow/{workflow_id}", workspaceId=workspace_id())["workflow"]["workflow"]
    ac = w.get("agent_config") or {}; llm = ac.get("llmConfig") or {}
    if (llm.get("provider"), llm.get("model")) != (AGENT_LLM["provider"], AGENT_LLM["model"]):
        ac["llmConfig"] = {**llm, **AGENT_LLM}; api("PUT", f"/api/v2/workflow/{workflow_id}", {"workflow": {**w, "agent_config": ac}})
    vs = api("GET", f"/api/v2/versions/workflow/{workflow_id}", workspaceId=workspace_id())["versions"]
    newest = max(vs, key=lambda v: v["versionNumber"])
    if not newest.get("isPublished"): api("POST", f"/api/v2/versions/workflow/{workflow_id}/publish", {"versionId": newest["id"]})
    return newest["versionNumber"]

"""Generate out/pl-g5-memo-raw.workflow.json from the rules of briefs/pl-g5-memo-raw.md.

Effective policy (the memo OM-3 of 3 February 2026 predates the CP-4 extract of 2 March 2026 and is replaced by it;
memo OM-17 of 9 October 2026 changes the extract):
  - callbacks: today or the next business day, 09:00 to 17:00 inclusive, later than `now`
  - deadline: early band (1-7 days late) 12th business day after today; late band (8-45) 6th business day
"""
import json
import pathlib

BASE = "https://freya-bank-mock.freyavoice.workers.dev/v1"
SLOT = "pl-g5-memo-raw"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ code shared by code steps

DATE_HELPERS = r'''
import datetime
import json
import re
HOL = ['2026-10-26', '2026-11-11', '2026-11-26', '2026-12-25', '2027-01-01']
DAYS = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
def parse_now(raw):
    raw = str(raw or '').strip().replace(' ', 'T')
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(raw[:16])
    except Exception:
        return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(raw[:10] + 'T00:00')
def isbd(d):
    return d.weekday() < 5 and d.isoformat() not in HOL
def kind(d):
    if d.isoformat() in HOL:
        return 'bank holiday, not a business day'
    if d.weekday() >= 5:
        return 'weekend, not a business day'
    return 'business day'
def nth_bd(start, n):
    d = start
    c = 0
    while c < n:
        d = d + datetime.timedelta(days=1)
        if isbd(d):
            c += 1
    return d
def next_bd(d):
    d = d + datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    while not isbd(d):
        d = d + datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    return d
def fmt(d):
    return DAYS[d.weekday()] + ' ' + str(d.day) + ' ' + d.strftime('%B %Y') + ' (' + d.isoformat() + ')'
def last_bd_of_week(monday):
    d = monday + datetime.timedelta(days=4)
    while d >= monday and not isbd(d):
        d = d - datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    return d if d >= monday else None
NOW = parse_now(vars.get('now'))
TODAY = NOW.date()
MONDAY = TODAY - datetime.timedelta(days=TODAY.weekday())
'''

SETUP_CODE = DATE_HELPERS + r'''
try:
    vars['today_text'] = fmt(TODAY) + ', ' + kind(TODAY)
    vars['now_time'] = NOW.strftime('%H:%M')
    lines = []
    for i in range(0, 35):
        d = TODAY + datetime.timedelta(days=i)
        lines.append(fmt(d) + ': ' + kind(d) + (' (today)' if i == 0 else ''))
    vars['calendar_text'] = '\n'.join(lines)
    words = []
    for i in range(7):
        this_d = MONDAY + datetime.timedelta(days=i)
        next_d = this_d + datetime.timedelta(days=7)
        words.append('"this ' + DAYS[i] + '" = ' + fmt(this_d) + ('' if this_d >= TODAY else ' (already past)') + '; "next ' + DAYS[i] + '" = ' + fmt(next_d))
    vars['weekday_words_text'] = '\n'.join(words)
    slots = []
    start = datetime.datetime.combine(TODAY, datetime.time(9, 0))
    end = datetime.datetime.combine(TODAY, datetime.time(17, 0))
    if NOW < end:
        first = start if NOW < start else NOW + datetime.timedelta(minutes=1)
        slots.append('today, ' + fmt(TODAY) + ', from ' + first.strftime('%H:%M') + ' to 17:00')
    nb = next_bd(TODAY)
    slots.append(fmt(nb) + ', from 09:00 to 17:00')
    vars['callback_slots_text'] = '; or '.join(slots)
    vars['setup_state'] = 'ok'
except Exception as e:
    vars['setup_state'] = 'error'
    vars['today_text'] = str(vars.get('now'))
    vars['now_time'] = ''
    vars['calendar_text'] = 'not available'
    vars['weekday_words_text'] = 'not available'
    vars['callback_slots_text'] = 'today or the next business day, from 09:00 to 17:00, later than now (' + str(vars.get('now')) + ')'
'''

ACCOUNT_CODE = DATE_HELPERS + r'''
def money(x):
    try:
        v = float(x)
    except Exception:
        return str(x)
    return ('%.2f' % v) if abs(v - round(v)) > 1e-9 else str(int(round(v)))
def products_from_vars():
    for key in ('products', 'load_account_response.data.products'):
        p = vars.get(key)
        if isinstance(p, str):
            try:
                p = json.loads(p)
            except Exception:
                p = None
        if isinstance(p, dict):
            p = [p]
        if isinstance(p, list) and p:
            return [x for x in p if isinstance(x, dict)]
    resp = vars.get('load_account_response')
    if isinstance(resp, dict):
        d = resp.get('data')
        if isinstance(d, dict) and isinstance(d.get('products'), list) and d.get('products'):
            return [x for x in d.get('products') if isinstance(x, dict)]
    pat = re.compile(r'^(?:products|load_account_response\.data\.products)(?:\.|\[)(\d+)\]?\.(\w+)$')
    found = dict()
    for k in list(vars.keys()):
        m = pat.match(str(k))
        if m:
            found.setdefault(int(m.group(1)), dict())[m.group(2)] = vars.get(k)
    return [found[i] for i in sorted(found)]
try:
    prods = products_from_vars()
    p = prods[0]
    ptype = str(p.get('type') or '')
    if ptype == 'credit_card':
        words = 'credit card ending ' + str(p.get('card_last4') or '')
        floor = p.get('minimum_payment')
        floor_name = 'the minimum payment'
    elif ptype == 'car_loan':
        words = 'car loan'
        floor = p.get('instalment_amount')
        floor_name = 'one instalment'
    else:
        words = 'personal loan'
        floor = p.get('instalment_amount')
        floor_name = 'one instalment'
    days_late = int(float(p.get('days_late')))
    past_due = float(p.get('past_due'))
    if days_late <= 7:
        band = 'early'
        deadline = nth_bd(TODAY, 12)
        attempts = 1
    else:
        band = 'late'
        deadline = nth_bd(TODAY, 6)
        attempts = 2
    valid = []
    d = TODAY
    while d <= deadline:
        if isbd(d):
            valid.append(fmt(d))
        d = d + datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    lb = last_bd_of_week(MONDAY)
    if lb is None or lb <= TODAY:
        lb = last_bd_of_week(MONDAY + datetime.timedelta(days=7))
    if lb > deadline:
        lb = deadline
    vars['product_words'] = words
    vars['product_type'] = ptype
    vars['product_id_text'] = str(p.get('product_id') or '')
    if len(prods) == 1 and p.get('product_id'):
        vars['product_id'] = str(p.get('product_id'))
    vars['past_due_text'] = money(past_due)
    vars['floor_text'] = money(floor)
    vars['floor_name'] = floor_name
    vars['days_late'] = str(days_late)
    vars['band'] = band
    vars['attempts'] = str(attempts)
    vars['deadline_text'] = fmt(deadline)
    vars['deadline_iso'] = deadline.isoformat()
    vars['valid_dates_text'] = '\n'.join(valid) if valid else 'none'
    vars['attempt1_text'] = fmt(lb)
    vars['today_is_business_day'] = 'yes' if isbd(TODAY) else 'no'
    other = ''
    if len(prods) > 1:
        other = ' Other late products in the record: ' + '; '.join(str(x.get('type')) + ' ' + str(x.get('product_id')) + ' past due ' + money(x.get('past_due')) for x in prods[1:])
    vars['other_products_text'] = other
    vars['account_state'] = 'ok'
except Exception as e:
    vars['account_state'] = 'error'
'''

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tool builders

HEADERS = {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}}


def api_tool(name, path, description, body_props, required, post_hook="", max_retries=0):
    props = {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"}}
    props.update(body_props)
    t = {
        "type": "function",
        "config": {"timeoutMs": 12000, "maxRetries": max_retries},
        "function": {
            "name": name,
            "handler": "__function__:api_call",
            "description": description,
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "url": {"type": "string", "default": BASE + path},
                    "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
                    "headers": HEADERS,
                    "body": {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required},
                },
            },
        },
    }
    if post_hook:
        t["post_process_code"] = post_hook
    return t


def hook(body):
    """A post-hook that drops headers and adds a what_to_do_next line built from `d` (the API body)."""
    return (
        "try:\n"
        "    if isinstance(result, dict):\n"
        "        result.pop('header', None)\n"
        "        d = result.get('data')\n"
        "        if not isinstance(d, dict):\n"
        "            d = dict()\n"
        "            result['data'] = d\n"
        "            d['ok'] = False\n"
        "            d['error'] = 'service failure'\n"
        + "\n".join("        " + line for line in body.strip("\n").split("\n")) + "\n"
        "except Exception:\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )


VERIFY_HOOK = hook(r'''
left = d.get('wrong_answers_left')
if d.get('hint') == 'day_month_swapped':
    msg = 'The day and the month seem to be the other way round. Ask the customer to say the month of their birth as a word, then call the tool again. This retry is not counted as a wrong answer.'
elif d.get('all_verified') is True:
    msg = 'Both security answers are correct.'
elif d.get('verified') is True:
    msg = 'Correct. Ask the next security question.'
elif d.get('ok') is False and not (isinstance(left, int) and left <= 0):
    msg = 'The answer could not be checked (' + str(d.get('error') or 'not readable') + '). It is not counted as a wrong answer. Ask the customer to say it again.'
elif isinstance(left, int) and left <= 0:
    msg = 'Three wrong answers. The identity check has failed. Do not state any account detail.'
else:
    msg = 'Wrong answer. Wrong answers left: ' + str(left) + '. Say that it does not match our records and ask the same question again.'
d['what_to_do_next'] = msg
''')

PROMISE_HOOK = hook(r'''
if d.get('ok') is True:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The promise is recorded.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The promise was NOT recorded (' + str(d.get('error') or 'error') + '). Never say it is recorded. If this is the first failure, call create_promise once more now with the same amount and date.'
''')

CALLBACK_HOOK = hook(r'''
if d.get('ok') is True:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The callback is booked.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The callback was NOT booked (' + str(d.get('error') or 'error') + '). Never say it is booked. If this is the first failure, call schedule_callback once more with the same date and time. If it failed twice, say you could not book the callback and call transition_to_farewell_no_callback.'
''')

TRANSFER_HOOK = hook(r'''
if d.get('ok') is True:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The transfer is done.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The transfer did NOT go through (' + str(d.get('error') or 'error') + '). Never say the customer is being connected. If this is the first failure, call the same transfer tool once more. If it failed twice, tell the customer you could not connect them.'
''')


def verify_tool(name, field, answer_desc):
    return api_tool(
        name, "/verify_identity",
        "Check the customer's " + ("date of birth" if field == "date_of_birth" else "last four phone digits")
        + ". CALL it every time the customer gives an answer to this question, one call per answer.",
        {
            "field": {"type": "string", "enum": ["date_of_birth", "phone_last4"], "default": field},
            "answer": {"type": "string", "default": "{{answer}}", "description": answer_desc},
        },
        ["customer_id", "field", "answer"], VERIFY_HOOK)


DOB_DESC = ("The date of birth as YYYY-MM-DD, whatever way the customer said it. Convert words to digits. "
            "A date given only as numbers is read as day, then month, then year (for example 03/07/1985 is 1985-07-03).")
PHONE_DESC = "Exactly four digits, the last four digits of the phone number on file, as the customer said them."


def transfer_tool(name, queue, trigger):
    return api_tool(
        name, "/transfer_to_agent", trigger,
        {"queue": {"type": "string", "enum": ["restructuring", "general", "support"], "default": queue}},
        ["customer_id", "queue"], TRANSFER_HOOK)


TRANSFER_HUMAN = transfer_tool(
    "transfer_human", "general",
    "Hand the call to a person (general queue). CALL it only when the customer asked for a human, you asked once whether you can help instead, and they still insist. "
    "In the same message tell them you are connecting them now.")
TRANSFER_SUPPORT = transfer_tool(
    "transfer_support", "support",
    "Hand the call to the customer support team. CALL it only when the customer mentioned illness, a death in the family or job loss, you offered the support team and they accepted. "
    "In the same message tell them you are connecting them now.")
TRANSFER_RESTRUCTURING = transfer_tool(
    "transfer_restructuring", "restructuring",
    "Hand the call to the restructuring team. CALL it when the customer asks for a new payment plan or lower instalments. Do not describe any plan. "
    "In the same message tell them you are connecting them now.")

CREATE_PROMISE = api_tool(
    "create_promise", "/create_promise",
    "Record the payment promise. CALL it only after you read back the product, the amount and the date, asked \"Do you confirm?\" and the customer gave a clear yes.",
    {
        "product_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{product_id}}", "description": "The product_id from the facts, copied unchanged."},
        "amount": {"type": "number", "default": "{{amount}}", "description": "The agreed amount, a number, from the floor up to the full past-due amount."},
        "date": {"type": "string", "default": "{{date}}", "description": "The agreed payment date as YYYY-MM-DD. Must be one of the valid promise dates."},
    },
    ["customer_id", "product_id", "amount", "date"], PROMISE_HOOK)

SCHEDULE_CALLBACK = api_tool(
    "schedule_callback", "/schedule_callback",
    "Book a callback for the customer. CALL it as soon as the person on the line names a day and time inside the allowed callback window.",
    {
        "date": {"type": "string", "default": "{{date}}", "description": "Callback date as YYYY-MM-DD: today or the next business day."},
        "time": {"type": "string", "default": "{{time}}", "description": "Callback time as HH:MM, 24 hour, from 09:00 to 17:00 and later than now."},
    },
    ["customer_id", "date", "time"], CALLBACK_HOOK)


def is_true(var):
    return {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
        {"variable": var, "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
        {"variable": var, "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}


def var_cond(var, op, operand=None):
    c = {"variable": var, "operator": op}
    if operand is not None:
        c["operand"] = operand
    return {"logic": "or", "conditions": [c]}


def to(target, desc, cond):
    return {"target_node": target, "description": desc, "condition": cond}


def tool_to(target, desc):
    return {"target_node": target, "description": desc, "is_tool_call": True,
            "condition": {"operator": "matches_intent", "description": desc}}


TRANSFER_ROUTES = [
    to("farewell_transferred_human", "The transfer to a person succeeded", is_true("transfer_human_response.data.ok")),
]
ALL_TRANSFER_ROUTES = TRANSFER_ROUTES + [
    to("farewell_transferred_support", "The transfer to support succeeded", is_true("transfer_support_response.data.ok")),
    to("farewell_transferred_restructuring", "The transfer to restructuring succeeded", is_true("transfer_restructuring_response.data.ok")),
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ prompts

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are Freya Bank's digital assistant on an outbound phone call. Freya Bank is calling the customer. Speak English. Keep every turn to one or two short sentences. Ask one question at a time.

Call facts: customer {{title}} {{first_name}} {{last_name}}. Current date and time: {{now}} ({{today_text}}). All date rules use this date, never the real clock.

Rules that hold in every step:
- Until both security answers have been verified, never say "collections", "debt", "payment", "late", "amount" or the product, and never say why you are calling. This applies to everyone, including relatives.
- If someone asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant, then continue with the current question.
- If someone asks "Is this a scam?", say they can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, then continue with the current question.
- If you are asked something you cannot answer from the tool results and the facts given to you, say you do not have that information. Never invent figures, dates or reasons.
- Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any other term.
- When a rule says to use a tool, call the tool. Saying that you did something is not doing it. Call one tool per message.
- After every tool result, follow its what_to_do_next and speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing.
- Never say something is recorded, booked or transferred unless the tool result says it worked.
- Tools named transition_to_farewell_... end the call: a fixed thank-you and goodbye is spoken for you after them. Call such a tool only when the rule says so, with no other tool in that message."""

OPENING_TASK = """You are on the line and have just introduced yourself and asked "Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?". Find out who is on the line. Do not call any bank tool in this step except transfer_human.

- Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name confirms that the customer is on the line. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not.
- If the answer does not confirm, ask "Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?" once more. If the person asked a question (robot, AI, scam, who is calling), answer it in one sentence first; the ask that follows is the second ask. If it is still unclear after the second ask, call transition_to_farewell_unclear.
- Say nothing about why you are calling.
- If the person says this number does not belong to {{title}} {{last_name}} (wrong number), call transition_to_farewell_wrong_number.
- If the person says {{title}} {{last_name}} has died, call transition_to_farewell_deceased and say nothing yourself.
- If the person says twice that they do not want to talk, call transition_to_farewell_declined.
- If the person asks for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call transfer_human."""

SOMEONE_ELSE_TASK = """The person on the line is not {{title}} {{last_name}}. Do not say why you are calling and say nothing about any account, even if they ask, offer to pay or say they are family. Do not ask them any security question. Ask when {{title}} {{last_name}} can be reached.

Allowed callback window: {{callback_slots_text}}. A callback must be today or the next business day, from 09:00 to 17:00 (both included), and later than now ({{now_time}}).
Calendar:
{{calendar_text}}

- When the person names a day and time inside the window, call schedule_callback with the date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the time (HH:MM, 24 hour). Do not read the booking back as done until the result says ok.
- If the person offers a day or time outside the window, say when callbacks are possible and ask once for another time. If the second answer is also outside the window, or they cannot give a time, do not book: call transition_to_farewell_no_callback.
- If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, call transition_to_farewell_wrong_number.
- If the person says the customer has died, call transition_to_farewell_deceased and say nothing yourself.
- If the person says that {{title}} {{last_name}} is now on the line or hands over the phone, call transition_to_opening."""

DOB_TASK = """{{title}} {{last_name}} confirmed who they are. You have asked for their date of birth as the first security question. You still may not say why you are calling.

- When the customer gives a date of birth, call verify_dob with it converted to YYYY-MM-DD. A date given only as numbers is day, then month, then year. Then follow what_to_do_next.
- A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total end the check.
- If the customer will not answer, or asks what the call is about instead of answering: the first time, explain that these questions protect their account and ask again. The second time (a second refusal or a second such question), call transition_to_farewell_declined.
- If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, call transition_to_farewell_declined.
- If the customer asks for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call transfer_human."""

PHONE_TASK = """The date of birth is verified. You have asked for the last four digits of the phone number on file. You still may not say why you are calling.

- When the customer gives four digits, call verify_phone with them. Then follow what_to_do_next.
- Wrong answers count together with any wrong date of birth: three in total end the check.
- If the customer will not answer, or asks what the call is about instead of answering: if you have not yet explained in this call that the questions protect their account, explain it once and ask again. Otherwise call transition_to_farewell_declined.
- If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, call transition_to_farewell_declined.
- If the customer asks for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call transfer_human."""

NEGOTIATE_TASK = """The customer is verified. You have stated the debt and asked "Can you make this payment today?". Your job: get a payment promise where you can, within the rules below.

FACTS (computed by the bank, use them exactly)
- Product: {{product_words}} (product_id {{product_id_text}}).{{other_products_text}}
- Full past-due amount: {{past_due_text}}. Floor amount: {{floor_text}} ({{floor_name}}).
- Days late: {{days_late}}. Band: {{band}}. Persuasion attempts allowed: {{attempts}}.
- Today: {{today_text}}.
- Deadline, the latest date you can record: {{deadline_text}}.
- Valid promise dates (today or later, business days, not after the deadline):
{{valid_dates_text}}
- Attempt 1 date: {{attempt1_text}}.
- Weekday words ("next <weekday>" is in the following calendar week, "this <weekday>" in the current week):
{{weekday_words_text}}
- Calendar:
{{calendar_text}}

TOOLS
- create_promise: only after the read-back and a clear yes.
- transfer_restructuring, transfer_support, transfer_human: only as the rules below say.
- transition_to_farewell_refused, transition_to_farewell_hardship, transition_to_farewell_dispute, transition_to_farewell_paid, transition_to_farewell_service_error: end the call as the rules say.

AMOUNTS
- Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". You propose every amount.
- If the customer says the full amount is too much: offer the floor amount, once, and say the rest stays overdue. If they refuse the floor, that is a flat refusal.
- If the customer proposes an amount from {{floor_text}} up to {{past_due_text}}, both included, accept it. Below {{floor_text}}: say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once; if they do not accept the floor, that is a flat refusal. Above {{past_due_text}}: the amount is {{past_due_text}}.

DATES
- A promise date must be one of the valid promise dates above.
- If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day.
- If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is {{deadline_text}} and offer it. If they refuse the deadline, that is a flat refusal.
- If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.
- A "yes" to paying today means today, if today is a valid promise date.
- A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with these rules.

FLAT REFUSALS AND PERSUASION
- A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.
- Attempt 1: propose the full past-due amount (or the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much) on {{attempt1_text}}.
- Attempt 2, only when attempts allowed is 2: propose the floor amount {{floor_text}} on the deadline {{deadline_text}}.
- When a flat refusal comes and all {{attempts}} attempt(s) are used, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Call transition_to_farewell_refused.
- If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, call transition_to_farewell_refused.

CONFIRMING
- Read back the product, the amount and the date, and ask "Do you confirm?". Call create_promise only after a clear yes.
- If the customer changes the date or the amount at this point, check the new value against these rules and read it back again.
- If create_promise fails, call it once more with the same values. Never say the promise is recorded unless the result says ok.

OTHER SITUATIONS (these come before persuasion)
- Illness, a death in the family or job loss: say one short sentence of sympathy, make no persuasion attempt, and offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call transfer_support. If they decline, call transition_to_farewell_hardship. If they still name a date or an amount themselves, record that promise under these rules.
- "I already paid" (this past-due amount): say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and call transition_to_farewell_paid.
- "This debt is not mine", "I never had this product", or the product was closed or paid off in the past: do not argue, take no promise, call transition_to_farewell_dispute.
- A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe any plan; call transfer_restructuring.
- A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call transfer_human.
- If a transfer fails twice, say you could not connect them. After a failed support transfer call transition_to_farewell_hardship; after a failed restructuring transfer call transition_to_farewell_service_error; after a failed human transfer continue helping."""

PROMISE_DONE_TASK = """The promise is recorded and you have said "You will receive a text message confirming this promise." and asked whether there is anything else.

- If the customer has nothing else, or says thanks or goodbye, call transition_to_farewell_promise.
- If they want to change or cancel the promise, say it cannot be changed in this call and they can change it in the mobile app. Then ask whether there is anything else.
- A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: call transfer_restructuring. Illness, a death in the family or job loss: one sentence of sympathy, offer the customer support team, and call transfer_support if they accept. A request for a human: ask once whether you can help, and call transfer_human if they insist.
- If a transfer fails twice, say you could not connect them and call transition_to_farewell_promise.
- Do not take another promise."""

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ closings

# farewell id -> (spoken farewell, close step)
FAREWELLS = {

    "farewell_account_error": ("I am sorry, I cannot reach your account details right now because of a technical problem. Thank you for your time. Goodbye.", "close_no_promise_service_error"),
    "farewell_failed": ("I am sorry, I could not verify your identity. Please use the Freya Bank mobile app or visit a branch. Thank you for your time. Goodbye.", "close_not_verified_failed"),
    "farewell_declined": ("I understand. Thank you for your time. Goodbye.", "close_not_verified_declined"),
    "farewell_callback": ("Thank you, we will call back then. Goodbye.", "close_not_reached_callback"),

CLOSES = {

FAREWELL_DESC = {

def end_node():
    return {
        "name": "hang_up", "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
        "disable_inactivity_monitor": True, "transitions": [],
        "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {
            "name": "call_closed", "handler": "__function__:end_call",
            "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}}}},
    }


def close_node(key, outcome, reason):
    body = {"outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": ["promise", "paid", "transferred", "no_promise", "not_verified", "not_reached"], "default": outcome}}
    if reason:
        body["reason"] = {"type": "string", "default": reason}
    tool = api_tool("close_call", "/close_call", "End the call record.", body, ["customer_id", "outcome"], max_retries=2)
    return {
        "name": key, "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": "hang_up",
        "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": True, "pre_actions": [tool],
        "transitions": [to("hang_up", "always", {"operator": "always"})],
    }


def farewell_node(key, text, close):
    return {
        "name": key, "node_type": "conversation", "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": close,
        "on_enter": {"type": "tts", "text": text}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": True,
        "task_message": "Say goodbye. Do not call any tool in this turn.",
        "transitions": [to(close, "always", {"operator": "always"})],
    }


def code_node(key, code, transitions, default):
    return {
        "name": key, "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": default,
        "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": True,
        "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {
            "name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
            "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                "code": {"type": "string", "default": code}, "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
        "transitions": transitions,
    }


def conv(key, task, tools, transitions, on_enter, max_turns, cap_target, extraction=None):
    n = {
        "name": key, "node_type": "conversation", "task_message": task, "tools": tools,
        "on_enter": on_enter, "on_enter_first_entry_only": False,
        "transitions": transitions, "max_node_turns": max_turns, "max_turn_transition": cap_target,
    }
    if extraction:
        n["extraction_schema"] = extraction
    return n


def build():
    nodes = {}
    nodes["setup"] = code_node("setup", SETUP_CODE, [to("opening", "always", {"operator": "always"})], "opening")

    nodes["opening"] = conv(
        "opening", OPENING_TASK, [TRANSFER_HUMAN],
        [
            to("ask_dob", "The customer confirmed they are on the line", var_cond("line_status", "equals", "confirmed")),
            to("someone_else", "Someone other than the customer answered", var_cond("line_status", "equals", "someone_else")),
        ] + TRANSFER_ROUTES + [
            tool_to("farewell_unclear", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_unclear"]),
            tool_to("farewell_wrong_number", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_wrong_number"]),
            tool_to("farewell_deceased", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_deceased"]),
            tool_to("farewell_declined", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_declined"]),
        ],
        {"type": "tts", "text": "Hello, I am a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and this call is recorded. Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?"},
        8, "farewell_unclear",
        extraction=[{
            "name": "line_status", "type": "string", "enum_values": ["confirmed", "someone_else"], "min_confidence": 0.7,
            "description": ("Who answered the assistant's question 'Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?'. "
                            "confirmed: the person clearly said yes, that's me, speaking, or their own name ({{first_name}} or {{last_name}}). "
                            "someone_else: the person said they are not the customer but someone else, for example a relative, a partner or a colleague, or that the customer is not available. "
                            "Leave empty for a greeting, 'go ahead', 'who is this', a question, a wrong number, a death, or anything unclear."),
        }],
    )

    nodes["someone_else"] = conv(
        "someone_else", SOMEONE_ELSE_TASK, [SCHEDULE_CALLBACK],
        [
            to("farewell_callback", "The callback was booked", is_true("schedule_callback_response.data.ok")),
            tool_to("farewell_no_callback", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_no_callback"]),
            tool_to("farewell_wrong_number", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_wrong_number"]),
            tool_to("farewell_deceased", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_deceased"]),
            tool_to("opening", "The customer has come to the phone"),
        ],
        {"type": "llm", "prompt": "Reply in one short sentence to what the person said and ask when {{title}} {{last_name}} can be reached. Do not say why you are calling. If they said the customer has died or that the number is wrong, call the matching transition tool instead."},
        12, "farewell_no_callback",
    )

    nodes["ask_dob"] = conv(
        "ask_dob", DOB_TASK, [verify_tool("verify_dob", "date_of_birth", DOB_DESC), TRANSFER_HUMAN],
        [
            to("ask_phone", "The date of birth was verified", is_true("verify_dob_response.data.verified")),
            to("farewell_failed", "Three wrong answers", var_cond("verify_dob_response.data.wrong_answers_left", "less_than", 1)),
        ] + TRANSFER_ROUTES + [tool_to("farewell_declined", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_declined"])],
        {"type": "tts", "text": "Thank you. Before we continue, I need to ask two security questions. What is your date of birth?"},
        15, "farewell_declined",
    )

    nodes["ask_phone"] = conv(
        "ask_phone", PHONE_TASK, [verify_tool("verify_phone", "phone_last4", PHONE_DESC), TRANSFER_HUMAN],
        [
            to("load_account", "Both answers were verified", {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
                {"variable": "verify_phone_response.data.all_verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
                {"variable": "verify_phone_response.data.all_verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"},
                {"variable": "verify_phone_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
                {"variable": "verify_phone_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}),
            to("farewell_failed", "Three wrong answers", var_cond("verify_phone_response.data.wrong_answers_left", "less_than", 1)),
        ] + TRANSFER_ROUTES + [tool_to("farewell_declined", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_declined"])],
        {"type": "tts", "text": "Thank you. What are the last four digits of the phone number we have on file for you?"},
        15, "farewell_declined",
    )

    get_account = api_tool("get_account", "/get_account", "Get the late products.", {}, ["customer_id"], max_retries=2)
    nodes["load_account"] = {
        "name": "load_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": True,
        "passthrough_default_transition": "prepare_account", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
        "disable_inactivity_monitor": True, "pre_actions": [get_account],
        "response_mapping": [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}],
        "transitions": [to("prepare_account", "always", {"operator": "always"})],
    }
    nodes["prepare_account"] = code_node(
        "prepare_account", ACCOUNT_CODE,
        [to("negotiate", "The account facts are ready", var_cond("account_state", "equals", "ok")),
         to("farewell_account_error", "always", {"operator": "always"})],
        "farewell_account_error")

    nodes["negotiate"] = conv(
        "negotiate", NEGOTIATE_TASK, [CREATE_PROMISE, TRANSFER_RESTRUCTURING, TRANSFER_SUPPORT, TRANSFER_HUMAN],
        [
            to("promise_recorded", "The promise was recorded", is_true("create_promise_response.data.ok")),
            to("farewell_promise_error", "Recording the promise failed twice", var_cond("create_promise_failure_count", "greater_than", 1)),
        ] + ALL_TRANSFER_ROUTES + [
            tool_to("farewell_refused", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_refused"]),
            tool_to("farewell_hardship", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_hardship"]),
            tool_to("farewell_dispute", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_dispute"]),
            tool_to("farewell_paid", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_paid"]),
            tool_to("farewell_service_error", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_service_error"]),
        ],
        {"type": "tts", "text": "Thank you, you are verified. I am calling from the collections team about a late payment on your {{product_words}}. The past-due amount is {{past_due_text}}, and it is {{days_late}} days late. Can you make this payment today?"},
        40, "farewell_refused",
    )

    nodes["promise_recorded"] = conv(
        "promise_recorded", PROMISE_DONE_TASK, [TRANSFER_RESTRUCTURING, TRANSFER_SUPPORT, TRANSFER_HUMAN],
        ALL_TRANSFER_ROUTES + [tool_to("farewell_promise", FAREWELL_DESC["farewell_promise"])],
        {"type": "tts", "text": "Your promise is recorded. You will receive a text message confirming this promise. Is there anything else I can help you with?"},
        8, "farewell_promise",
    )

    for key, (text, close) in FAREWELLS.items():
        nodes[key] = farewell_node(key, text, close)
    for key, (outcome, reason) in CLOSES.items():
        nodes[key] = close_node(key, outcome, reason)
    nodes["hang_up"] = end_node()

    return {
        "initial_node": "setup",
        "system_prompt": SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        "nodes": nodes,
        "global_nodes": {},
        "test_variables": {"customer_id": "c_test", "first_name": "Daniel", "last_name": "Reyes", "title": "Mr", "now": "2026-10-14T11:00"},
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    out = root / "out" / (SLOT + ".workflow.json")
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(build(), indent=1))
    print(out)
